presented_options.A: 0 = OK, 1 = SQL error, 2 = CLI usage error, 3 = storage/IO error
presented_options.B: 0 = OK, 1 = any error (SQL, CLI, or IO collapsed together), with stderr distinguishing the category
presented_options.C: 0 = OK, 1 = SQL error, 2 = storage/IO, 3 = CLI usage (CLI last because it's the rarest)

answers.rationale: exit_code() maps Usage->2, Io/Storage/Serde->3, Parse/Type/Sql->1; main returns 0 on Ok.

presented_options.A: statements inherit the transaction of the previous BEGIN if any was ever opened in the session
presented_options.B: statements run under a long-running implicit transaction that commits only when the process exits
presented_options.C: statements run without any transaction; durability is deferred to a periodic checkpoint
presented_options.D: each statement is implicitly wrapped in its own transaction that commits on success, matching BEGIN/COMMIT semantics

answers.rationale: with_auto_tx checks in_transaction(); if not, it does begin/execute/commit, so each standalone statement gets its own implicit transaction.

presented_options.A: synchronous double-write: every page is written to a scratch region before being written to its home location
presented_options.B: shadow paging: mutations go to a copy page; a pointer swap at commit promotes the copy atomically
presented_options.C: an append-only write-ahead log, replayed at startup to re-apply committed transactions and drop the uncommitted suffix
presented_options.D: ARIES-style WAL with explicit undo and redo records plus a separate dirty-page table checkpoint

answers.rationale: Recovery reads the checkpoint file then replays committed WAL records; uncommitted transactions are dropped. README confirms append-only WAL.

presented_options.A: each record carries a CRC32; replay stops at the first record whose CRC fails to verify
presented_options.B: no per-record check; a single CRC covers the whole WAL file on clean shutdown
presented_options.C: records are padded to a fixed 512-byte sector boundary; partial sectors are discarded
presented_options.D: records are written in pairs (main + mirror); replay prefers whichever pair verifies

answers.rationale: Each WAL record is serialized, length-prefixed, then followed by a per-record CRC32; read_all verifies each record's CRC and returns an error on mismatch.

presented_options.A: vectorised/columnar execution where each operator produces and consumes batches of column vectors
presented_options.B: materialising execution: each operator fully computes its output set before the next operator starts reading
presented_options.C: push-based execution where operators drive their children forward via a single dataflow scheduler
presented_options.D: a Volcano-style iterator tree: each operator exposes open/next/close and returns one row (or tiny batch) at a time

answers.rationale: The PhysicalOperator trait exposes open/next/close; each operator returns one ExecRow at a time via next(), which is the Volcano iterator model.

presented_options.A: a B-tree keyed by the composite (index_key, row_id); duplicates are naturally ordered by row_id
presented_options.B: a hash map keyed by the indexed value alone; collisions chain a Vec<RowId>
presented_options.C: an inverted list built lazily on first query and cached in memory
presented_options.D: a bitmap per distinct value; looked up with bitwise AND for compound predicates

answers.rationale: BTreeIndex.map is BTreeMap<String, Vec<u64>> keyed by the indexed value's key() string, with duplicate row IDs chaining in a Vec.

presented_options.A: Update and Delete are distinct operators rather than one 'Mutate' operator parameterised by a kind
presented_options.B: SeqScan, IndexScan, Filter, Project, NestedLoopJoin, Sort, Limit, Insert, Update, Delete each as a distinct type
presented_options.C: IndexScan and SeqScan as two variants of a single ScanKind enum so the executor only has one Scan operator
presented_options.D: Filter and Project exist as separate types rather than being fused into one 'SelectExpr' operator

answers.rationale: SeqScan and IndexScan are separate struct types in exec.rs and separate PhysicalPlan variants in plan.rs, not two variants of one ScanKind enum.

presented_options.A: inside the storage layer, which transparently redirects SeqScan calls through the index when available
presented_options.B: inside the planner when lowering the logical plan to a physical plan; the parser only produces ASTs
presented_options.C: inside the executor at open() time, after consulting the catalog to see whether an index is applicable
presented_options.D: inside the parser, encoded as a special AST node when the WHERE clause mentions an indexed column

answers.rationale: scan_for_table is called from the planner's plan_select method; it consults the catalog for an index and emits IndexScan or SeqScan accordingly.

presented_options.A: errors are propagated via panics with typed payloads and caught at the CLI via std::panic::catch_unwind
presented_options.B: errors are encoded as strings (Result<T, String>) so every caller formats them uniformly
presented_options.C: each subsystem defines its own error type; the CLI sees a Box<dyn Error> and pattern-matches on downcast
presented_options.D: a single crate-wide error enum with one variant per source is the return type of top-level entry points; lower modules convert at their public boundary

answers.rationale: MiniDbError is a single crate-wide enum with variants Usage, Io, Parse, Type, Sql, Storage, Serde; top-level functions return Result<T, MiniDbError>.

presented_options.A: table / json / messagepack selectable only via an environment variable MINIDB_FORMAT
presented_options.B: the format is fixed at build time via a Cargo feature (--features=json)
presented_options.C: table output only; downstream callers are expected to parse and re-format it themselves
presented_options.D: table / csv / json selectable via a --format CLI flag or a .format meta-command in the REPL

answers.rationale: OutputFormat has Table/Csv/Json variants; --format CLI flag selects it, and .format meta-command can change it at runtime.

presented_options.A: --quiet suppresses the per-statement summary entirely; stdout still carries the data stream
presented_options.B: per-statement summary lines (e.g. `ok 3 rows`) go to stderr, letting callers pipe stdout straight into another tool
presented_options.C: the per-statement summary is written to stdout immediately before the data so callers see it arrive first
presented_options.D: when --format json is active, the JSON value is the only thing on stdout — no banner lines, no trailing 'ok' line

answers.rationale: print_summary writes to stderr via eprintln!, so a summary on stdout before data would be inconsistent with the actual stderr separation.

presented_options.A: pages are a mixed size; the header chooses between 4 KiB and 16 KiB per table based on row width
presented_options.B: the page size is a single compile-time constant referenced throughout storage
presented_options.C: pages are identified by a newtype over u64 (PageId) rather than a bare integer
presented_options.D: the heap stores rows inside fixed-size pages rather than one file per row

answers.rationale: PAGE_SIZE is a single compile-time constant (4096) used throughout storage; mixed-size pages would be inconsistent.

presented_options.A: all three rows — every fsynced WAL record is replayed on startup
presented_options.B: the two earliest rows — only WAL records that survive the CRC check are replayed; the trailing one is dropped
presented_options.C: an error at startup demanding manual recovery before any SELECT can run
presented_options.D: no rows — a transaction whose WAL trail has no COMMIT record is treated as an uncommitted prefix and discarded

answers.rationale: committed_ops only moves WAL entries to committed when a Commit record is seen; without it the transaction stays pending and is never replayed.

presented_options.A: hits only in `parser` and `error`, where the modules format diagnostic messages directly
presented_options.B: zero hits — every diagnostic outside the CLI boundary goes through the `log` facade
presented_options.C: scattered hits across most modules; the codebase routinely uses `eprintln!` for diagnostics
presented_options.D: a small number of hits inside `exec` operators, used to print per-row debugging during EXPLAIN

answers.rationale: No eprintln! appears in any file outside src/main.rs and src/cli.rs; all non-CLI code returns errors via Result.

presented_options.A: executes the SELECT and silently falls back to the default `table` format
presented_options.B: panics with an unwrap on the unrecognised format string
presented_options.C: exits with code 1 and prints a SQL error pointing at the SELECT
presented_options.D: exits with code 2 and prints a CLI usage error on stderr naming the bad value

answers.rationale: OutputFormat uses clap ValueEnum; an unrecognized --format value causes clap to print a usage error to stderr and exit with code 2.
